title: Integrations
description: The three targets that needed no exporter: Caddy and MinIO already spoke Prometheus and were switched on, and the recommendation service was instrumented in its own code.

panels.title: Edge requests / sec
panels.description: Every request that reaches the stack, including the Vue app and its assets. The backend never sees these, so this is the only place total site traffic exists.

panels.title: Edge p95
panels.description: Latency measured at the proxy, so it includes TLS and the trip to the upstream — always a little above the backend's own p95.

panels.title: Caddy config
panels.description: Whether Caddy's last configuration reload succeeded. A failed reload leaves the previous config running, which otherwise looks like an edit that did nothing.

panels.title: MinIO health
panels.description: MinIO's own view of whether the cluster is serving.

panels.title: Objects stored
panels.description: Objects across all buckets — one per uploaded avatar.

panels.title: Storage free
panels.description: Usable free space MinIO reports. It sits on the same disk the host panel watches, so these two run out together.

panels.title: Requests / sec by server
panels.description: srv0 is the :8080 HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, srv1 the :8443 application origin, srv2 the metrics site this panel is drawn from.

panels.title: Responses / sec by status
panels.description: The edge's view of what users actually received — including responses the backend never produced, such as the 404 Caddy returns for /api/metrics.

panels.title: Edge latency percentiles
panels.description: Time to first byte at the proxy. Compare against the backend's own percentiles: a gap that only appears here is TLS or proxying, not the app.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Requests the proxy is holding open right now.

panels.title: Bytes served
panels.description: Response size through the edge. Its own panel rather than sharing an axis with the request rate above — bytes and requests are not the same unit.

panels.title: Upstream health
panels.description: Caddy's own check on the services it proxies to. Zero means it has stopped being able to reach one.

panels.title: Capacity
panels.description: Usable rather than raw: raw counts the erasure-coding overhead, usable is what objects can actually take.

panels.title: S3 requests / sec by operation
panels.description: getobject and putobject are avatar reads and writes; headbucket is the backend's startup check that the bucket exists.

panels.title: S3 errors / sec
panels.description: Rejected-auth is the one to watch here: it means something is calling MinIO with credentials it does not have.

panels.title: S3 traffic
panels.description: Bytes in and out of object storage.

panels.title: Objects & buckets
panels.description: Both counts, so one axis.

panels.title: Drives & nodes
panels.description: Online against offline. A single-node MinIO has one of each, so this is a liveness check more than a capacity one.

panels.title: Requests / sec by endpoint and status
panels.description: The recommendation service measuring itself. The Dependencies dashboard shows the same calls as the backend sees them — a gap between the two is time lost in the network or in the client's own timeout.

panels.title: Latency percentiles
panels.description: Measured inside the service, so it excludes the network hop the backend's own recommender timings include.

panels.title: Latency by endpoint
panels.description: /feed blocks a browsing user. /signal is fire-and-forget and should stay far below it.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident set. This service loads NumPy, SciPy and an SVD model, so it is the heaviest thing in the stack and the likeliest OOM candidate.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cores used. A retrain is CPU-bound and shows up here as a spike.

panels.title: Python GC collections / sec
panels.description: Collections per generation. Generation 2 is the expensive one.
